source.exact_title: Dapagliflozin in Heart Failure: A Comprehensive Meta-analysis on Functional Capacity, Symptoms, and Safety Outcomes
source.source_type: systematic review and conventional meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials

sections_or_headings: 2.5 Risk of Bias and Quality Assessment
4.3 Agreement and Disagreement with Previous Studies
coverage_decision: All main-text figures and tables were visually inspected and represented as structured blocks. References were extracted separately to Markdown. No supplement was present in the source folder.
omissions: Bibliography entries were not atomized solely as citations.
The final reproduction-rights notice page contains no substantive scientific content.
source_consistency_findings: Figure 1 and the Results narrative state 10 included studies. Table 1 and Figure 2 also show 10 study rows, but Table 2 additionally contains Wiviott 2019/DECLARE baseline rows that are not represented in Table 1, the risk-of-bias figure, or outcome forests and would vastly exceed the reported N=12,695 if treated as part of the pooled HF population.
Section 3.3 states nine trials had overall some-concerns risk of bias and two had low risk (11 total), while Figure 2 shows eight some-concerns plus two low-risk trials (10 total).

The Methods correctly specify mean difference for continuous outcomes and Figures 3-4 label mean difference, but the Abstract and Results prose repeatedly call the 6MWD and KCCQ pooled estimates risk ratios.
The Abstract reports adverse events as RR 0.96 with 95% CI 0.98-1.03, an internally impossible interval for that estimate; Section 3.5.3 and Figure 7 report RR 0.98 (95% CI 0.93-1.03).
Discussion section 4.3.1 describes a significant decrease in overall adverse-event risk, whereas the review's own pooled adverse-event result is nonsignificant (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.93-1.03; p=0.39).
The conclusion language about mortality benefit across all ranges of heart failure is stronger than the subgroup result: HFrEF mortality was significant, HFpEF mortality was not.
